Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]), the choice hypothesis of the cited tensor construction. **(b) Declared species and sector.** A **declared species sector** of the model consists of: a nonzero separable complex Hilbert space $H$, the **one-particle space** of the species, as assigned in P1; a mass parameter $m>0$ in kg; a spin label $s\in\{0,\tfrac12,1,\tfrac32,\dots\}$ and the internal factor $V_{s}=\mathbb C^{2s+1}$ of P6 clause (ii), with the **orbital factor** $H_{\mathrm{sp}}$ the factor carrying no internal degree of freedom when the one-particle space is given as a completed product $H_{\mathrm{sp}}\widehat\otimes V_{s}$; for the massive spin-$s$ model of [[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] the one-particle space is $L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{2s+1})$, whose spin components are the internal factor of P6 clause (ii) in the reading of that definition; a **statistics choice** $\sigma\in\{+,-\}$, where $+$ declares the species **bosonic** and $-$ declares it **fermionic**; and, for a charged species, a charge parameter $q\in\mathbb R$ in coulombs. The parameters and the statistics choice are empirical model assignments with their uncertainties, in the sense of P6 clause (iii); no value and no statistics choice is derived by this definition. **(c) The $n$-particle sector.** Fix $n\ge1$. The **labelled $n$-particle space** of the species is the $n$-fold completed tensor power $H^{\otimes n}$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]), whose tensor factors are mathematical labels and not observable particle identities, equipped with the permutation unitaries $(U_\pi)_{\pi\in S_n}$ and the sector projections $P_\sigma^{(n)}$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-permutation-sector-projections]]), where $P_+^{(n)}$ is the symmetrizing projection and $P_-^{(n)}$ the alternating projection. The **$n$-particle sector space** of the declared species is $$\mathfrak H_n^\sigma:=\operatorname{ran}P_\sigma^{(n)}\ \subseteq\ H^{\otimes n},$$ a closed linear subspace carrying the inner product of $H^{\otimes n}$; on it every permutation acts by the scalar $$U_\pi|_{\mathfrak H_n^\sigma}=\operatorname{sgn}_\sigma(\pi)\, \mathrm{id}_{\mathfrak H_n^\sigma},\qquad \operatorname{sgn}_+(\pi)=1,\quad \operatorname{sgn}_-(\pi)=\operatorname{sgn}(\pi),$$ by clause (c) of the cited permutation lemma. For $n=1$ one has $\mathfrak H_1^+=\mathfrak H_1^-=H$. **(d) Declared sector preparations.** A **declared sector preparation** of $n$ particles of the species is a state of the framework on the sector space, that is a density operator $$\rho\in D(\mathfrak H_n^\sigma)$$ in the sense of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]] and clause (a) of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]], read as the state assigned to the preparation by P1 clause (iii). A **pure sector preparation** is a pure state, i.e. the rank-one operator of a unit ray of $\mathfrak H_n^\sigma$; a statistical mixture of sector preparations is a convex combination. The sector is part of the declaration of the species: a model that declares one statistics choice does not switch it within the same declaration. **(e) Sector quantities.** Let $A$ be a linear operator on the labelled space $H^{\otimes n}$ with domain $D(A)$. The model reads $A$ as a **quantity of the declared sector** only when $A$ **preserves the sector**, $$P_\sigma^{(n)}D(A)\subseteq D(A),\qquad A\,\mathfrak H_n^\sigma\subseteq \mathfrak H_n^\sigma,$$ in which case the **sector restriction** $A_\sigma:=A|_{\mathfrak H_n^\sigma}$ with domain $D(A)\cap\mathfrak H_n^\sigma$ is part of the declaration and is the quantity actually read on sector preparations; a bounded quantity preserves the sector exactly when it commutes with $P_\sigma^{(n)}$. An operator that does not preserve the sector is not read on the sector; in particular no quantity of a single labelled factor is assumed to define a quantity of the sector unless it preserves it. If $A_\sigma$ is self-adjoint, its outcome law in a sector preparation is the law of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] read on $\mathfrak H_n^\sigma$. **(f) Status and scope.** Clauses (a)-(e) fix the vocabulary with which the framework reads the adopted P6 assumptions: they add no assumption to P1 and P6, and the permutation invariance of sector preparations and of sector readouts is a conditional consequence proved on this page ([[pthm-nrqm-identical-particles-permutation-invariance]]), not a content of this definition. Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be a complex Hilbert space with inner product linear in the first argument ([[def-hilbert-space]], [[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]), let $H\widehat\otimes H$ be its completed tensor square with inclusion $\kappa$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]), and for $n=2$ let $(U_\pi)_{\pi\in S_2}$ and the projections $P_\pm^{(2)}$ be those of [[lem-nrqm-composites-permutation-sector-projections]]. Write $\tau:=U_{(12)}$ for the **exchange operator**, so that $\tau\bigl(\kappa(u\otimes v)\bigr)=\kappa(v\otimes u)$ for $u,v\in H$; in the sequel the inclusion is suppressed and $u\otimes v$ denotes $\kappa(u\otimes v)$. Then: (a) $\tau$ is self-adjoint and $\tau^2=I$; consequently $\tau$ is an isometry with $\tau^{-1}=\tau=\tau^{*}$ ([[def-hilbert-space-adjoint]], [[def-bounded-linear-operator]]); (b) $P_+^{(2)}=\tfrac12(I+\tau)$ and $P_-^{(2)}=\tfrac12(I-\tau)$, and $$\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(2)}=\{x\in H\widehat\otimes H:\tau x=x\},\qquad \operatorname{ran}P_-^{(2)}=\{x\in H\widehat\otimes H:\tau x=-x\};$$ (c) for all $u,v\in H$, $$\|u\otimes v+v\otimes u\|^{2}=2\bigl(\|u\|^{2}\|v\|^{2}+|\langle u,v\rangle|^{2}\bigr), \qquad \|u\otimes v-v\otimes u\|^{2}=2\bigl(\|u\|^{2}\|v\|^{2}-|\langle u,v\rangle|^{2}\bigr);$$ in particular, if $u,v$ are orthonormal, then $s:=\tfrac1{\sqrt2}(u\otimes v+v\otimes u)$ and $a:=\tfrac1{\sqrt2}(u\otimes v-v\otimes u)$ are orthonormal, $\tau s=s$ and $\tau a=-a$, and both $\operatorname{ran}P_\pm^{(2)}$ are nonzero; (d) whenever $u,v\in H$ are orthonormal, $\tau\kappa(u\otimes v)\ne\kappa(u\otimes v)$. Consequently, if $H$ contains an orthonormal pair (equivalently, $\dim H\ge2$), both exchange eigenspaces contain nonzero vectors and $\tau\ne I$. If $H=\{0\}$ or $\dim H=1$, then $\tau=I$, $P_+^{(2)}=I$ and $P_-^{(2)}=0$; for $H=\{0\}$ the tensor square and both ranges are zero.

derivations.claim: [Decomposition of the internal factor] By [F3] the antisymmetric combination $\sigma_-$ spans $W_0$ and $\sigma_+,\ e_+\otimes e_+,\ e_-\otimes e_-$ span the three-dimensional space $W_1$; since $e_+\otimes e_--e_-\otimes e_+$ is antisymmetric under the exchange and $e_+\otimes e_+,e_-\otimes e_-,e_+\otimes e_-+e_-\otimes e_+$ are symmetric, $\operatorname{ran}P_-^{(V)}=\mathbb C(e_+\otimes e_--e_-\otimes e_+)=\mathbb C\Psi=W_0$ and $\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(V)}=\operatorname{Sym}^2V=W_1$; the two subspaces are orthogonal complements of each other because $V\otimes V=W_0\oplus W_1$. [F3, F4, algebra]

[Sector decomposition] By [F2] the unitary image of the sector is $\bigl(\operatorname{ran}P_-^{(K)}\otimes\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(V)}\bigr)+\bigl(\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(K)}\otimes\operatorname{ran}P_-^{(V)}\bigr)$, an orthogonal direct sum, and step 1.1 identifies its summands as the spin-triplet part $\operatorname{ran}P_-^{(K)}\otimes W_1$ and the spin-singlet part $\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(K)}\otimes W_0$; by [F5] the singlet part has dimension $\dim\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(K)}=\binom{m+1}2$, and the triplet part has dimension $3\dim\operatorname{ran}P_-^{(K)}=3\binom m2$; this is (a) up to the assignment of the names singlet and triplet, which is the naming of $W_0$ and $W_1$ in [F3]. [F2, F3, F5, step 1.1, algebra]

[Opposite symmetry] The identity of (b) is the vector identity of [F2] under the identifications of steps 1.1 and 2.1: the first summand carries the internal factor in $\operatorname{ran}P_-^{(V)}=W_0$, the singlet, and the orbital factor in $\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(K)}$, the symmetric orbital component, while the second summand carries the internal factor in $\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(V)}=W_1$, the triplet, and the orbital factor in $\operatorname{ran}P_-^{(K)}$, the antisymmetric orbital component. This proves (b). [F2, step 1.1, step 2.1, algebra]

[Parallel spins] Let $u,v$ be orthonormal and $\chi$ a unit vector. By [F4] one has $P_-^{(V)}(\chi\otimes\chi)=0$ and $P_+^{(V)}(\chi\otimes\chi)=\chi\otimes\chi$; hence the identity of (b) gives $\Theta P_-^{(K\otimes V)}\bigl((u\otimes\chi)\otimes(v\otimes\chi)\bigr)=P_-^{(K)}(u\otimes v)\otimes(\chi\otimes\chi)$, and multiplying by $\sqrt2$ gives the unit vector $(u\wedge v)\otimes(\chi\otimes\chi)$ because $\|u\wedge v\|=1$ and $\|\chi\otimes\chi\|=1$ by [F4]; both vectors lie in the sector and both rays are declared pure sector preparations by [F1], so the images of the two rays coincide, which is (c). citations.quote: Adopt the state and composition postulate P1 ([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]]) and the identical-particle and spin postulate P6 ([[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]]) in the readings of [[def-nrqm-identical-particles-framework-species-sectors-and-preparations]], and assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Declare a **spin-half fermionic species** whose one-particle space is the completed product $K\widehat\otimes V$ of a nonzero finite-dimensional complex Hilbert space $K$ (the orbital factor) with $V=\mathbb C^{2}$ (the internal factor of P6 clause (ii) for $s=\tfrac12$), with $V$ carrying the orthonormal basis $(e_{+},e_{-})$ of [[pthm-nrqm-angular-momentum-two-spin-composition]], and declare $n=2$ particles in the adopted antisymmetric sector $$\mathfrak H_2^-=\operatorname{ran}P_-^{(K\otimes V)}\subseteq (K\otimes V)\widehat\otimes(K\otimes V)$$ of the declared species, with the regrouping unitary $\Theta$ of [[thm-nrqm-identical-particles-two-factor-symmetry-decomposition]]. Write $u\wedge v:=\sqrt2\,P_-^{(K)}(u\otimes v)$ and $u\odot v:=\sqrt2\,P_+^{(K)}(u\otimes v)$ for $u,v\in K$, and $\sigma_\pm:=(e_+\otimes e_-\pm e_-\otimes e_+)/\sqrt2$ for the spin combinations. Then, as conditional statements of the declared model: (a) *sector decomposition*: $\Theta$ carries $\mathfrak H_2^-$ onto the orthogonal direct sum $\bigl(\operatorname{ran}P_-^{(K)}\otimes\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(V)}\bigr)+\bigl(\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(K)}\otimes\operatorname{ran}P_-^{(V)}\bigr)$, where $\operatorname{ran}P_-^{(V)}=\mathbb C\Psi$ is the one-dimensional spin-singlet line spanned by the singlet $\Psi$ of [[pthm-nrqm-angular-momentum-two-spin-composition]] clause (d) and $\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(V)}=W_{1}$ is the three-dimensional spin-triplet space of that theorem; consequently the antisymmetric two-particle sector is the sum of a **spin-singlet part** $\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(K)}\otimes\mathbb C\Psi$, of dimension $\binom{m+1}2$ for $m=\dim K$, with symmetric orbital factor, and a **spin-triplet part** $\operatorname{ran}P_-^{(K)}\otimes W_1$, of dimension $3\binom m2$, with antisymmetric orbital factor; (b) *opposite orbital symmetry*: for all $u,v\in K$ and $\chi,\chi'\in V$, $$\Theta\Bigl(P_-^{(K\otimes V)}\bigl((u\otimes\chi)\otimes(v\otimes\chi')\bigr)\Bigr) =P_+^{(K)}(u\otimes v)\otimes P_-^{(V)}(\chi\otimes\chi') +P_-^{(K)}(u\otimes v)\otimes P_+^{(V)}(\chi\otimes\chi');$$ the spin-singlet component therefore multiplies the symmetric orbital component and the spin-triplet component multiplies the antisymmetric orbital component, so within each component the orbital exchange symmetry is opposite to the spin exchange symmetry; (c) *parallel spins*: if $u,v\in K$ are orthonormal and $\chi\in V$ is a unit vector, then $\Theta$ carries the ray of $P_-^{(K\otimes V)}\bigl((u\otimes\chi)\otimes(v\otimes\chi)\bigr)$ to the ray of $P_-^{(K)}(u\otimes v)\otimes(\chi\otimes\chi)$, whose unit representative is $(u\wedge v)\otimes(\chi\otimes\chi)$; The model assignment of the antisymmetric sector is that of P6; the statements above are conditional on it and assert no spin-statistics theorem, no interaction, no dynamics and no measurement.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $H$ be a complex Hilbert space with completed tensor powers $H^{\otimes n}$ and symmetric projections $P_\pm^{(n)}$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-permutation-sector-projections]]). Then: (a) *Slater vectors*: for $n\ge2$ and orthonormal $u_1,\dots,u_n\in H$, the Slater vector $$S(u_1,\dots,u_n):=\frac1{\sqrt{n!}}\sum_{\sigma\in S_n}\operatorname{sgn}(\sigma)\,u_{\sigma(1)}\otimes\cdots\otimes u_{\sigma(n)}$$ satisfies $\|S(u_1,\dots,u_n)\|=1$ and $S(u_1,\dots,u_n)=\sqrt{n!}\,P_-^{(n)}(u_1\otimes\cdots\otimes u_n)$; (b) *exclusion*: if $u_i=u_j$ for some $i\ne j$, then $P_-^{(n)}(u_1\otimes\cdots\otimes u_n)=0$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-permutation-sector-projections]] (d)); (c) *two orbitals, bounded pair interaction*: let $u,v\in L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$ be normalized and orthogonal, let $W:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R$ be measurable and bounded with $W(-z)=W(z)$ for a.e. $z$, let $\Theta:L^2(\mathbb R^3)\otimes L^2(\mathbb R^3)\to L^2(\mathbb R^6)$ be the Euclidean product unitary ([[lem-nrqm-composites-euclidean-l2-product-unitary]]), put $\varphi_\pm:=(u\otimes v\pm v\otimes u)/\sqrt2$ and $$D:=\int_{\mathbb R^6}|u(x)|^2|v(y)|^2W(x-y)\,dx\,dy,\qquad X:=\int_{\mathbb R^6}\overline{u(x)}v(x)u(y)\overline{v(y)}\,W(x-y)\,dx\,dy,$$ integrals of absolutely integrable functions. Then $D,X\in\mathbb R$ and the pair expectation of the multiplier $M_W$ in the two spatial states is $$\bigl\langle M_W(\Theta\varphi_\pm),\Theta\varphi_\pm\bigr\rangle=D\pm X .$$ (d) *repulsive Coulomb exchange*: let $\kappa>0$, $W(z)=\kappa/|z|$, let $u,v\in W^{1,2}(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)\cap L^2$ be normalized and orthogonal ([[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]], [[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]]). The vectors $\Theta\varphi_\pm$ belong to $D(M_W)$: Hardy translated in the $y$ variable and Tonelli give $\iint|u(x)v(y)|^2/|x-y|^2\le4\|u\|_2^2\|\nabla v\|_2^2<\infty$, and the swapped product has the same property. Then the integrals $D$ and $X$ converge absolutely, $0\le D<\infty$, $X\in\mathbb R$ with $X\ge0$; consequently $D-X\le D+X$, i.e. the antisymmetric spatial pair state has the lower expectation of the repulsive Coulomb pair interaction. The exchange calculation is a statement about the indicated spatial vectors; it does not deduce the spin-statistics assignment of any species, and combining the spatial states with spin requires a separately stipulated symmetry rule. No physical interpretation of $D$, $X$ or the states is asserted.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be a complex Hilbert space with inner product linear in the first argument ([[def-hilbert-space]], [[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]), let $H\widehat\otimes H$ be its completed tensor square with inclusion $\kappa$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]), and for $n=2$ let $(U_\pi)_{\pi\in S_2}$ and the projections $P_\pm^{(2)}$ be those of [[lem-nrqm-composites-permutation-sector-projections]]. Write $\tau:=U_{(12)}$ for the **exchange operator**, so that $\tau\bigl(\kappa(u\otimes v)\bigr)=\kappa(v\otimes u)$ for $u,v\in H$; in the sequel the inclusion is suppressed and $u\otimes v$ denotes $\kappa(u\otimes v)$. Then: (a) $\tau$ is self-adjoint and $\tau^2=I$; consequently $\tau$ is an isometry with $\tau^{-1}=\tau=\tau^{*}$ ([[def-hilbert-space-adjoint]], [[def-bounded-linear-operator]]); (b) $P_+^{(2)}=\tfrac12(I+\tau)$ and $P_-^{(2)}=\tfrac12(I-\tau)$, and $$\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(2)}=\{x\in H\widehat\otimes H:\tau x=x\},\qquad \operatorname{ran}P_-^{(2)}=\{x\in H\widehat\otimes H:\tau x=-x\};$$ (c) for all $u,v\in H$, $$\|u\otimes v+v\otimes u\|^{2}=2\bigl(\|u\|^{2}\|v\|^{2}+|\langle u,v\rangle|^{2}\bigr), \qquad \|u\otimes v-v\otimes u\|^{2}=2\bigl(\|u\|^{2}\|v\|^{2}-|\langle u,v\rangle|^{2}\bigr);$$ in particular, if $u,v$ are orthonormal, then $s:=\tfrac1{\sqrt2}(u\otimes v+v\otimes u)$ and $a:=\tfrac1{\sqrt2}(u\otimes v-v\otimes u)$ are orthonormal, $\tau s=s$ and $\tau a=-a$, and both $\operatorname{ran}P_\pm^{(2)}$ are nonzero; (d) whenever $u,v\in H$ are orthonormal, $\tau\kappa(u\otimes v)\ne\kappa(u\otimes v)$. Consequently, if $H$ contains an orthonormal pair (equivalently, $\dim H\ge2$), both exchange eigenspaces contain nonzero vectors and $\tau\ne I$. The notation $H\widehat{\otimes}K:=\widehat{H\odot K}$ is used in the rest of this pair. No assertion is made about unbounded operators or algebraic sums of non-completed tensor products.

Define, for finite sums, $$\Bigl\langle\sum_i u_i\otimes v_i,\ \sum_j u'_j\otimes v'_j\Bigr\rangle:=\sum_{i,j}\langle u_i,u'_j\rangle_H\,\langle v_i,v'_j\rangle_K .$$ Then: (a) *well-definedness and sesquilinearity*: the displayed value is independent of the representatives of its two arguments and defines a Hermitian sesquilinear form on $H\odot K$, linear in the first argument and conjugate-linear in the second; (b) *positive definiteness and orthonormal coordinates*: $\langle z,z\rangle\ge0$ for every $z\in H\odot K$, with $\langle z,z\rangle=0$ exactly for $z=0$; more precisely, if $U_0\subseteq H$ and $V_0\subseteq K$ are finite-dimensional subspaces with orthonormal bases $e_1,\dots,e_p$ and $f_1,\dots,f_q$, then every $z$ in the span of the elementary tensors from $U_0\times V_0$ has a unique expansion $z=\sum_{a,b}c_{ab}\,e_a\otimes f_b$ and $\langle z,z\rangle=\sum_{a,b}|c_{ab}|^2$; in particular the assignment is an inner product on $H\odot K$; (c) *completion*: the norm completion $(\widehat{H\odot K},\kappa)$ of $H\odot K$ ([[def-completion-of-a-normed-space]]) exists and, with the unique inner product extending the given one, is a complex Hilbert space; $\kappa$ is a linear isometry with dense image, $\|\kappa(u\otimes v)\|=\|u\|\,\|v\|$, and any two completions of $H\odot K$ are identified by a unique surjective linear isometry fixing $H\odot K$ pointwise; (d) *product bases*: if $(e_a)_{a\in A}$ and $(f_b)_{b\in B}$ are orthonormal families in $H$ and $K$ whose closed linear spans are $H$ and $K$, then $(\kappa(e_a\otimes f_b))_{(a,b)\in A\times B}$ is an orthonormal family in $\widehat{H\odot K}$ whose closed linear span is $\widehat{H\odot K}$; if $A$ and $B$ are countable then $\widehat{H\odot K}$ is separable.
